'''John William Mullin''' (22 August 1925 – 11 March 2009) was a [[Ramsay Memorial Professor of Chemical Engineering]] and world expert in [[crystallization|crystallisation]].<ref name=Times>{{cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/professor-john-mullin-professor-of-chemical-engineering-lrdrgh985sh|title=Obituary: Professor John Mullin: professor of chemical engineering|work=[[The Times]]|date=26 May 2009|access-date =23 April 2021}}</ref><ref name=TCE>The Chemical Engineer, May 2009 page 58, John William Mullin, 1925-2009</ref>

==Education and career==

Between 1945 and 1948 Mullin was with the [[Royal Air Force|RAF]]. After leaving the RAF, he studied at the [[University of Wales]] and gained a first class degree in [[chemistry]] in 1951.<ref name=Times/> Mullin's joined the [[University College London]], where he completed a postgraduate diploma in [[chemical engineering]] in 1952, and then a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1955.<ref name=Peppasone>{{cite book|title=One Hundred Years of Chemical Engineering|author=N. Peppas|page=235|date=30 April 1989|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0792301455}}</ref> He achieved a [[Doctor of Science|DSc]] from the [[University of Wales]] in 1962.<ref name=Times/>

In 1956, he joined the Ramsay department of chemical engineering  at [[University College London]], first as a lecturer, and from 1961 as a reader, before becoming a professor in 1969.<ref name=Peppasone/> While under [[M. B. Donald]], the Ramsay professor of chemical engineering, Mullin's built a strong research group in the field of crystallisation.<ref>{{cite book|title=One Hundred Years of Chemical Engineering|author=N. Peppas|page=234|date=30 April 1989|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0792301455}}</ref> His textbook ''Crystallization'' was first published in 1961.<ref name=Times/> Due to his expertise into [[Crystallization|cystallisation]] he was in demand as a consultant in the chemical, petrochemical, food and pharmaceutical industries.<ref name=Times/>

In 1985, he was appointed the Ramsay professor of chemical engineering, replacing the previous incumbent [[P. N. Rowe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/chemical-engineering/about/history|title=History|website=UCL|date=19 July 2018 |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> He retired from the role in 1990, being replaced by A. Cornish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/2009-deaths|title=2009 Deaths|website=UCL|date=2 July 2018 |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> He continued as [[Professor Emeritus]] and in 1997 was UCL Crabtree Foundation president.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/crabtree/officers|title=Officers of the Foundation|website=UCL|date=5 December 2018 |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref>

Upon Mullin's death, Professor Richard Allsop wrote for the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]],

''"As well as being eminent in his field, John Mullin was a valued senior colleague to many of us at UCL across and probably well beyond the Faculty of Engineering. He lived and thrived, and helped us to live and thrive, through times of immense change in academic life by his leadership in the senior roles he played, and by real personal concern for many with whom he worked. In retirement we continued to see him often, and we shall continue to feel his presence in spirit."''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/appreciation-of-past-fellows?y=2009&p=3|title=Appreciations of Past Fellows|website=Royal Academy of Engineering|access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 1970, Mullin was jointly awarded the IChemE Moulton Medal with J Nyvlt for the most meritorious paper published by the Institution.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icheme.org/knowledge/medals-and-prizes/publications/moulton-medals/|title=Moulton Medals|website=IChemE|access-date=20 April 2021}}</ref>

Mullin was elected as Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]; the [[Institution of Chemical Engineers]] and the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]]. He was also an honorary Fellow of the School of Pharmacy; [[University College Wales]] and [[University College London]].<ref name=Times/>

==Early and personal life==
Mullin was born in [[Cheshire]] on 22 August 1925, attending the [[Hawarden High School]] until 1940. He met his wife Averil while at the [[University of Wales]], and they would go onto have two children, Jonathan and Susan, and grandchildren Victoria and Katherine. Mullin died on 11 March 2009 at home aged 83.<ref>{{cite news|title=Notices|work=[[The Times]]|date=14 March 2009}}</ref>
